subject: Microphone capture was mis-packed (TX port 16-bit in a 24-bit stream); earlier mic-based speaker levels are unreliable
device: LG Fx0, Nura v26.06, kernel r29 (fx0-linux integration/fx0-txsb-format)

finding.symptom: With the back ends pinned to 24-bit (since r24), every captured sample had its low 16 bits zero: only bits 23:16 varied (8 significant bits), giving noise-like data around -13 to -20 dBFS in a quiet room.
finding.cause: WCD9306 CDC_CONN_TX_SB_Bn_CTL bits 5:4 hold each TX port's sample format (0 = 24-bit, 2 = 16-bit), like the RX ports. The driver (as the downstream tapan init table) set all TX ports to 16-bit (0x20) and never changed it; live registers read 0x28 (DEC1 + 16-bit).
finding.fix: fx0-linux 'ASoC: codecs: wcd9306: Program the TX port sample format' sets the TX format from hw_params. After it the registers read 0x08 and the data carries about 13 significant bits (bits 23:11).

after_fix.speaker_tone_at_mic: 1 kHz tone at 0.7 FS through RX3 picked up at -4.5 dBFS (digital volume 84) and -14.2 dBFS (74), a 9.7 dB step for 10 dB; gone (-62 dBFS) with SPK DAC off. The earlier '-52 dBFS' speaker readings came from the mis-packed capture and do not measure level.
open: Capture still not clean: low 11 bits always zero and a quiet-room level near -23 dBFS
Playback stopped reaching the mic after two or three play/record cycles in one session and was absent in a following session; cause unknown
Whether the speaker is now audible needs the owner's ears (r25 stock-register values plus r29)

ucm: A 'Mic' UCM device (local/mic/HiFi.conf.with-mic) gave PipeWire a working 'Main microphone' source, but it is held back and the packaged UCM restored until capture data is clean
